observation: [measured] sIPSC mean amplitude 57.3 -> 27.5 pA (-52%, own arithmetic); KS on events p 9e-135; 14 cells/7 animals vs 9/5; 140 mM KCl, -70 mV, no antagonist
compatible_explanations: E1 (if a high-amplitude input class is lost); E2; E3
weakened_explanations: E6 (smaller KO cells would be better clamped, not worse; opposite sign of the sEPSC amplitude change); E4 (not testable: pipette sets E_Cl near 0)
why: [inferred] The cumulative curve shows the KO lacking the large events (control tail to about -150 pA): a mean fall can come from fewer large inputs (E1), smaller quanta (E2) or fewer or less responsive receptors (E3). Mean amplitude alone does not separate them.
discriminating_measure: mIPSC amplitude and CV in TTX, same internal; amplitude distribution of unitary events by paired recording or minimal stimulation; response to a puffed GABA-A agonist in TTX
what_each_outcome_would_favour: Smaller mIPSC with normal agonist response -> E2 (supply); smaller mIPSC and smaller agonist response -> E3; loss of only the large-event class with unchanged small events -> E1; normal mIPSC -> the sIPSC change is network-driven (E5) or detection (artefact)
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: Decides whether a supply lever (reuptake, transaminase) or a receptor lever (positive modulator) is interpretable at all; E1 would make both act on a smaller input set

observation: [measured] sIPSC mean frequency 10.3 -> 8.4 Hz (-18%, own arithmetic); SD above the mean; significance only by KS on pooled distribution (p 9.4e-8); no per-cell or per-animal test
compatible_explanations: all of E1-E6 (a small fall is compatible with each)
weakened_explanations: none is excluded; E1 as the sole cause is made less likely only if the fall is real, which is not shown at animal level
why: [measured]+[inferred] A fall by a fifth is small against the spread. [inferred] An amplitude-dependent detection threshold (4 x SD of filtered trace) lowers the detected frequency when events shrink, so frequency and amplitude are not independent readouts.
discriminating_measure: per-cell frequency in TTX-free and TTX conditions; frequency analysed at one fixed absolute amplitude threshold in both genotypes; animal-level mixed model
what_each_outcome_would_favour: Frequency unchanged at fixed threshold -> E1 weakened, E2/E3 favoured; frequency down in mIPSC -> E1 or E2 (presynaptic); both unchanged -> artefact of detection
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: If frequency is unchanged, interneuron-number or firing explanations drop, and the question narrows to quantal size or receptors; if down, any lever acting on the synapse acts on fewer synapses

observation: [measured] sIPSC internal solution 140 mM KCl (about 144 mM Cl, own arithmetic); E_Cl about 0 mV by Nernst with about 130 mM external Cl; events recorded at -70 mV are inward and enhanced
compatible_explanations: E1, E2, E3, E6 (events are amplitude-maximised and read conductance)
weakened_explanations: E4 (chloride gradient is set by the pipette and is not measured; this recording cannot test it); E5 only indirectly
why: [measured] the authors state the high-chloride solution 'enhances the chemical gradient'. [inferred] amplitude then reflects conductance, not the native driving force.
discriminating_measure: gramicidin-perforated patch for E_GABA by genotype in the same cell class, against rest, threshold and input conductance; K-gluconate-internal sIPSC (outward at -70 mV, small)
what_each_outcome_would_favour: E_GABA near rest or above threshold in KO but not in control -> E4; E_GABA equal -> E4 dropped for this phenotype
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: Decides chloride-transport levers and the sign of any GABA-supply or receptor lever; a depolarising KO gradient makes boosting GABA conditional

observation: [declared] no miniature IPSC (TTX) recording; mEPSC was recorded with TTX
why: [measured by string search of the article body] 'mIPSC' does not occur; the TTX arm exists only for glutamatergic events. The pre-versus-postsynaptic test the authors applied to excitation was not applied to inhibition.
discriminating_measure: mIPSC amplitude and frequency in TTX, same cells as sIPSC
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: Required before any presynaptic (supply) versus postsynaptic (receptor) lever is chosen

observation: [declared] no evoked IPSC, no paired-pulse ratio, no failure rate, no unitary IPSC
why: [measured by string search] the only evoked recordings are field responses (Supp S3, Fig 5).
discriminating_measure: evoked IPSC input-output with PPR and minimal-stimulation failures
what_each_outcome_would_favour: low PPR/high failures -> E2 (release probability); normal PPR with smaller IPSC -> E3 or E1
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: separates a release-probability lever from a receptor lever

observation: [declared] no GABA-A antagonist or glutamate-receptor antagonist named for sIPSC; at -70 mV in KCl, EPSCs are inward as well. [measured] sEPSC KO mean amplitude 24.7 pA and frequency 10.1 Hz are close to the KO 'sIPSC' 27.5 pA and 8.4 Hz
compatible_explanations: all, conditional on the events being GABAergic (unverified)
why: [inferred] If the KO event set contains glutamatergic events, the 'inhibitory' fall could reflect loss of a large GABAergic component from a mixed set. The numerical proximity of KO sIPSC and sEPSC values is a hint, not a finding.
discriminating_measure: bath gabazine or bicuculline on sIPSC; NBQX/APV on the same recording; fraction of events abolished by genotype
what_each_outcome_would_favour: fraction blocked by a GABA-A antagonist differs by genotype -> the event set was mixed and every amplitude and frequency figure above is of a mixture
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: Decides whether the defect reads GABA-A at all; without it no GABA-A, supply or chloride lever has a measured target

observation: [measured] interneuron AP amplitude 60.78 -> 45.03 mV (-26%) in 5/4 vs 6/5 cells/animals; AP half-width 0.7 -> 0.55 ms; AP counts versus current not significantly different; interneuron class not determined
compatible_explanations: E1/E2 (smaller presynaptic spikes could release less); E5 (maturation, myelination, authors' discussion)
weakened_explanations: none excluded; n too small for a negative
why: [authors' interpretation] 'could be related to reduced action-potential amplitude'. [inferred] Five and six cells of unknown class cannot represent the inhibitory input to layer II/III pyramidal cells.
discriminating_measure: paired recordings or optogenetic stimulation of a defined interneuron class with the unitary IPSC; AP amplitude per class
what_each_outcome_would_favour: AP amplitude down in the class that supplies the IPSCs and unitary IPSC down -> presynaptic route; unchanged -> not the cause
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: If presynaptic, a postsynaptic receptor lever starts from normal receptors and may add little; a supply lever acts on a weakened release

observation: [measured] pyramidal input resistance 102.88 -> 143.03 Mohm (+39%); resting potential -79.25 -> -73.62 mV (5.6 mV depolarised); sag and rebound larger; HT carries several of these (Rin, rest, sag) without a significant rebound; dispersion type not declared in Table 1
compatible_explanations: E5, E6 (cell size or leak could change input resistance); also E4 if rest sets the driving force
weakened_explanations: E3 as the sole explanation of the synaptic data does not explain the intrinsic changes
why: [inferred] Higher input resistance and depolarisation are passive or channel properties of the same cells; they bear on excitability and on the driving force for GABA at rest, not on the amplitude of a voltage-clamped IPSC.
discriminating_measure: passive properties (Rin, Cm, Rs) of the same cells whose IPSC is recorded; recording at matched potential
what_each_outcome_would_favour: IPSC amplitude correlates with Cm or Rs across cells in both genotypes -> E6; no correlation -> E6 not the driver
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: An excitability lever (K+ conductance, Ih) has a measured passive correlate; a synaptic lever does not

observation: [measured] sEPSC amplitude 23.3 -> 24.7 pA (+6%) by printed means; mEPSC amplitude shifted up by KS; mEPSC decay unchanged; mEPSC frequency not different from S-HT but differs from S-WT
compatible_explanations: E3 for excitation (authors: postsynaptic); not informative for inhibition
weakened_explanations: E6 as a common recording artefact (excitatory and inhibitory amplitudes move in opposite directions)
why: [inferred] Opposite signs argue against one geometric or clamp artefact scaling every current, but the excitatory shift is 6% in printed means.
discriminating_measure: same cells, same internal: mIPSC and mEPSC amplitude and Rs
what_each_outcome_would_favour: opposite shifts hold with matched Rs -> not a global scaling
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: none directly; keeps an AMPA/NMDA lever and a GABA lever as separate questions

observation: [measured] bursts in 36/42 KO, 4/23 HT, 0/11 WT slices (24, 14, 7 animals); whole-cell sIPSC/sEPSC recordings are separate; [declared] no statement whether burst epochs were excluded; burst current at -70 mV is several hundred pA (Supp S2, opened)
compatible_explanations: E5 (network state alters or contaminates the synaptic data)
weakened_explanations: E1-E3 are not excluded; E5 is not proven
why: [inferred] 86% of KO slices burst, so the KO sIPSC set was probably recorded in a network that bursts; whether the sIPSC is a cause of the bursting or a consequence is not separable in this design. HT slices burst in 17%, and sIPSC for HT alone is not reported.
discriminating_measure: sIPSC in KO slices that do not burst (6/42 in this dataset) versus bursting ones; HT versus WT sIPSC; TTX-block or Mg/NMDAR-quiet epochs; age series before bursts appear
what_each_outcome_would_favour: IPSC deficit also in non-bursting KO slices and in HT/KO before bursts -> upstream of network state; deficit only in bursting slices -> E5
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: If E5, GABA or receptor levers treat a consequence; a lever on bursting itself (NMDAR, excitability) is the interpretable comparison

observation: [measured] burst reversal potential: whole burst -31 +/- 9.5 mV, onset +6 +/- 11.6, high-frequency part -36 +/- 9.8 mV (30 bursts, 5 animals); internal solution not stated for this experiment
compatible_explanations: E5; inhibition still engaged during bursts (a mixed E/I reversal)
weakened_explanations: a complete loss of GABA conductance during the burst is not supported by a reversal well below 0 mV (conditional on the internal)
why: [authors' interpretation] excitation dominates at onset. [inferred] reversal depends on the internal chloride, which is unspecified for this experiment; it cannot be read as a chloride gradient.
discriminating_measure: same experiment with the internal stated and with gabazine; GABA conductance during the burst by dynamic clamp
what_each_outcome_would_favour: reversal shifts positive with gabazine -> inhibition present in the burst
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: speaks to whether potentiating residual inhibition has something to act on during the event

observation: [measured] d-APV (50 uM) abolishes bursts in 5 slices/3 animals; the delayed field response (Supp S3) is NMDAR-dependent; no GABA-A antagonist was applied to WT slices to ask whether blocked inhibition produces the same bursts
compatible_explanations: E5 (NMDAR-dependent network event); consistent with any E1-E4 upstream cause of reduced inhibition (burst needs NMDAR whatever triggers it)
weakened_explanations: none excluded; d-APV does not discriminate inhibitory explanations
why: [inferred] NMDAR dependence of the burst says what sustains it, not why the threshold is lower.
discriminating_measure: gabazine or a GABA-A antagonist in WT slices at matched network state; NMDAR antagonist in KO plus GABA-A modulation
what_each_outcome_would_favour: WT slices burst under partial GABA-A block like KO -> reduced inhibition sufficient; not -> other lowering of threshold needed
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: NMDAR block is the one pharmacological arm already shown to stop the endpoint in WWOX slices (tool, generic); it is the comparator for any inhibitory lever

observation: [measured] carbenoxolone 100 uM lowers burst frequency by 87% and duration by 18%, not reversed on washout; brilliant blue FCF 10 uM no suppression
compatible_explanations: non-discriminating (CBX also blocks NMDAR, authors' discussion)
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: none (dropped as a lever, see levers_notes)

observation: [measured] age P13-P17; mice die at 3-4 weeks (authors); E_GABA in WT cortex of the same age from one other-model paper (reader finding: about -67 mV at P13-17, n=5, pooled regions, other mouse models) sits above the Wwox resting potentials
compatible_explanations: E4 and E5 (developmental chloride shift, late maturation)
why: [reused reading, transferred] depolarising but possibly shunting GABA; the sign is not binary. No E_GABA exists for any Wwox tissue.
discriminating_measure: E_GABA by gramicidin-perforated patch at P11, P13-17 by genotype in the recorded cell class, with input conductance
what_each_outcome_would_favour: E_GABA more positive in KO than control -> E4/E5 (immature or altered chloride); equal -> not a chloride phenotype
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: sets whether GABA potentiation (supply or receptor) is conditional on depolarisation; whether chloride transport is a lever

observation: [measured] Synapsin-I-Cre conditional line with Cre-positive littermate controls; [declared] no Cre-negative flox group, no recombination read-out, no glial or interneuron-class specificity shown
compatible_explanations: E1-E3 as neuron-autonomous or network effects of neuronal Wwox loss
weakened_explanations: glial contributions are weakened by design (Synapsin-Cre) but not excluded (Cre in glia not tested)
why: [inferred] pre- and postsynaptic neurons are both targeted, so the line cannot separate presynaptic from postsynaptic cell autonomy; the global knockout (survival 3-4 weeks) is a different model.
discriminating_measure: interneuron-class-specific deletion or pyramidal-specific deletion; Cre reporter
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: transfer of any finding to the global knockout or to patients is an extra step; every lever statement is in the Synapsin-Cre model

observation: [measured] mEPSC/sEPSC/sIPSC tests are KS tests whose unit is undeclared; IT36 audit: 10 of 18 printed KS p values are below the one-value-per-cell floor, so events are probably the unit; no animal-level statistic for synaptic currents; sIPSC control component counts (7+7 cells, 4+4 animals) do not equal the printed pooled counts (14 cells, 7 animals)
why: [inferred] a mean over events nested in 9 KO cells from 5 animals gives no animal-level effect size.
discriminating_measure: re-analysis with animal as unit, mixed-effects model; raw event tables (not available)
what_each_outcome_would_favour: effect holds at animal level -> the phenotype is robust enough to design from; not -> abstain
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: sets the strength with which any lever is anchored to this deficit

observation: [measured] hippocampal slices show no spontaneous activity; CA1 to CA3 PS larger in KO; CA3 to CA1 unchanged
weakened_explanations: a global brain-wide defect of inhibition
why: [inferred] the bursting phenotype is neocortical in this preparation; the inhibitory recordings are neocortical only; hippocampal interneuron loss is a different-model finding (reused).
discriminating_measure: sIPSC in hippocampal CA1 in the same mice
what_each_outcome_would_favour: IPSC deficit also in hippocampus without bursts -> not tied to network state
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: limits transfer of any inhibitory lever to one region and stage

observation: [measured] heterozygote: bursts in 4/23 slices; Rin, rest and sag significantly different from WT; rebound not; sIPSC for HT versus WT not reported (S-CTL pools them)
source_row: SR01, SR33, SR35, SR39, SR41, SR18
compatible_explanations: E5, intrinsic change graded by dose
why: [inferred] a graded dose pattern in intrinsic properties and burst incidence while the inhibitory data are pooled leaves the synaptic dose-response unknown.
discriminating_measure: sIPSC WT versus HT versus KO analysed separately, animal-level
what_each_outcome_would_favour: IPSC graded in HT -> inhibition tracks dose and bursting; ungraded -> separate
pharmacological_decision_it_would_change: a dose-graded defect supports a lever that restores quantity; an all-or-none one does not
